# The clippy row's baseline: the findings the release already has. The row applies the cut's rule
# (Cut7's kit clippy gate: a crate fails only on findings beyond what its base already has) without
# linting the base a second time: a crate reads FAIL for each finding beyond this file, KNOWN when
# its findings are within it, and names each line whose count fell here with the line that
# replaces it (or "delete its line"), which the next change of this file takes.
#
# One line a finding kind: crate<TAB>file<TAB>lint code<TAB>count<TAB>message. The lint code is the
# diagnostic's code.code from `cargo clippy --message-format=json`; the message has no line or
# column; the count is the number of places (file, line, column) with that code and message. A
# compile error with no code (rustc gives a syntax error none) is never a line here: its target was
# not linted, so it always fails the crate.
#
# To regenerate it from a release: dispatch sami-checks on the release commit, download that run's
# sc-res-clippy artifact, and take its clippy-findings.txt (the same format, every finding of the
# six crates). Drop the lines of findings being fixed, keep this header, and commit.
#
# From run 45380232583 on 509a2d77 (Cut8's release), less its 3 function_casts_as_integer findings,
# which are being fixed.
